processed_hadiths.english_translation: Chapter on Qirad (Mudaraba/Profit-sharing Partnership) in Goods

potential_issues.issue: This is a chapter header, not a hadith narration
potential_issues.impact: No chain of transmission or textual content to analyze

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Malik: It is not proper for anyone to engage in muqarada (profit-sharing partnership) except with cash money, because muqarada in goods is not proper. This is because muqarada in goods can only be in one of two ways: Either the owner of the goods says to him: 'Take this good and sell it, then buy and sell with its price on the basis of qirad,' so the owner of the capital has stipulated an advantage for himself from selling his commodity and what suffices him from its maintenance. Or he says: 'Buy and sell with this commodity, and when you are finished, buy me a similar good to what I gave you. If there is any surplus, it is between me and you.' Perhaps the owner of the goods gives it to the worker at a time when it is in demand with a high price, then the worker returns it when it has become cheap, buying it for a third of its price or less. Thus the worker would have profited half of what decreased from the price of the goods in his share of the profit. Or he takes the goods at a time when its price is low, then works with it until much wealth accumulates in his hands, then that good becomes expensive and its price rises when he returns it, so he buys it with all that is in his hands, and his work and effort go in vain. This is uncertainty (gharar) which is not proper. If this is done in ignorance until it is completed, then the measure of the wage of the one to whom the qirad was given for selling it and his effort should be considered and given to him, then the wealth becomes qirad from the day the wealth became liquid and gathered as cash, and it is returned to a qirad like it.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Chapter on Rent/Transportation Costs in Qirad

potential_issues.issue: This is a chapter header, not a hadith narration
potential_issues.impact: No chain of transmission or textual content to analyze

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Malik regarding a man who gave another man wealth as qirad, and he bought goods with it, then transported it to a trading town, but it was unsellable and he feared loss if he sold it. So he hired transportation to another town and sold it at a loss, and the transportation cost consumed the entire capital. Malik said: If what he sold was sufficient to pay for the transportation, then that is the way. But if anything remains from the transportation cost after the original capital, it is upon the worker, and nothing from it is upon the owner of the capital to be pursued. That is because the owner of the capital only ordered him to trade with his wealth, so the muqarid does not pursue him with anything beyond that wealth. If that were to be pursued from the owner of the capital, that would be a debt upon him from other than the wealth in which he gave him qirad. So the muqarid cannot impose that upon the owner of the capital.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Malik regarding a man who gave another man wealth as qirad, and he worked with it and profited, then bought from the profit of the wealth or from its totality a slave-girl and had intercourse with her and she became pregnant from him, then the wealth decreased. Malik said: If he has wealth, the value of the slave-girl is taken from his wealth to compensate the capital. If there is surplus after the capital is fulfilled, it is between them according to the original qirad. And if he does not have sufficient means, the slave-girl is sold until the capital is compensated from her price. Malik said regarding a man who gave another man wealth as qirad, and he transgressed and bought with it a commodity and added to its price from his own means: The owner of the capital has the choice - if the commodity is sold with profit or loss or is not sold - if he wishes to take the commodity, he takes it and pays him what he advanced in it. And if he refuses, the muqarid becomes his partner with his portion of the price in the growth and decrease according to the measure of what the worker added to it from his own means. Malik said regarding a man who took wealth from another man as qirad, then gave it to another man to work with as qirad without the permission of its owner: He is guarantor for the wealth. If it decreases, the decrease is upon him, and if it profits, the owner of the wealth has his stipulated portion from the profit, then the one who worked has his stipulated portion from what remains of the wealth. Malik said regarding a man who transgressed and borrowed from what is in his hands from the qirad some wealth and bought with it a commodity for himself: If he profited, the profit is according to their stipulation in the qirad, and if it decreased, he is guarantor for the decrease. Malik said regarding a man who gave another man wealth as qirad, and the one to whom the wealth was given borrowed from it some wealth and bought with it a commodity for himself: The owner of the capital has the choice - if he wishes, he partners with him in the commodity according to its qirad terms, and if he wishes, he leaves it between him and it, and takes from him the entire capital. And likewise is done with everyone who transgresses.

السِّلْعَةِ عَلَى قِرَاضِهَا ، وَإِنْ شَاءَ خَلَّى بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا ، وَأَخَذَ مِنْهُ رَأْسَ الْمَالِ كُلَّهُ ، وَكَذَلِكَ يُفْعَلُ بِكُلِّ مَنْ تَعَدَّى /10 . #E364

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Malik regarding a man who gave another man wealth as qirad: When the wealth is substantial enough to bear the expenses, if the worker travels with it, he may eat from it and clothe himself reasonably according to the amount of the wealth, and hire from the wealth - when it is substantial and he cannot handle it alone - some of those who can assist him with some of its burden. Among the works are works that the one who takes the wealth does not do, and his like does not do them, such as collecting debts, transporting goods, tying them, and similar things. So he may hire from the wealth someone who suffices him in that. The muqarid may not spend from the wealth nor clothe himself from it as long as he is residing with his family. Expenses are only permissible for him when he travels with the wealth and the wealth can bear the expenses. If he only trades with the wealth in the town where he resides, he has no expenses from the wealth nor clothing. Malik said regarding a man who gave another man wealth as qirad, and he went out with it and with his own wealth: He allocates the expenses from the qirad and from his wealth according to the proportions of the wealth.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Malik regarding a man who has qirad wealth and he spends from it and clothes himself from it: He does not give gifts from it, nor give to a beggar or anyone else from it, nor reciprocate favors with it to anyone. But if he gathers with people and they brought food and he brought food, I hope that would be permissible if he did not intend to show favor over them. But if he intended that or what resembles it without the permission of the owner of the capital, then he must seek absolution of that from the owner of the capital. If he absolves him of that, there is no harm in it. But if he refuses to absolve him, then he must reciprocate with the like of that, if that is something that has reciprocation.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Malik: The matter agreed upon among us regarding a man who gave another man wealth as qirad, and he bought goods with it, then sold the goods on credit and profited in the wealth, then the one who took the wealth died before he collected the wealth - if his heirs want to collect that wealth while they are on the stipulation of their father from the profit, that is for them if they are trustworthy over that. If they dislike collecting it and leave it between the owner of the capital and it, they are not obligated to collect it, and nothing is upon them nor for them if they hand it over to the owner of the capital. But if they collect it, they have from it the stipulation and expenses like what their father had in that - they are in it in the position of their father. If they are not trustworthy over that, they may bring a trustworthy agent to collect that wealth. When he collects all the wealth and all the profit, they are in that in the position of their father. Malik said regarding a man who gave another man wealth as qirad on condition that he works with it, and whatever he sells from it on credit, he is guarantor for it: That is binding upon him - if he sells on credit, he has guaranteed it.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Malik regarding a man who gave another man wealth as qirad, and the worker borrowed an advance from the owner of the capital, or the owner of the capital borrowed an advance from him, or the owner of the capital consigned with him a consignment to sell for him, or with dinars to buy a commodity for him with them. Malik said: If the owner of the capital only consigned with him while knowing that if his wealth were not with him, then he asked him for the like of that, he would do it out of brotherhood between them or because of the ease of that burden upon him, and if he refused that, he would not withdraw his wealth from him. Or if the worker only borrowed from the owner of the capital or carried his consignment while knowing that if his wealth were not with him, he would do the like of that for him, and if he refused that, he would not return his wealth to him. So when that is confirmed from both of them, and that was from them on the basis of kindness, and it was not a condition in the original qirad, then that is permissible, there is no harm in it. But if a condition entered into that, or it is feared that the worker only did that for the owner of the capital so that he would keep his wealth in his hands, or the owner of the capital only did that so that the worker would hold his wealth and not return it to him, then that is not permissible in qirad, and it is what the people of knowledge forbid.
